Thanks again for the time today, Sam — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Recap: We discussed your latency/throughput SLOs for the customer-facing chat product (p95 <250ms target, p99 <400ms preferred) and your desire to validate cost + latency tradeoffs across vendors. You shared a representative request corpus and noted that peak concurrent load will be ~2k qps during flash traffic.
- What we (Redwood) will do: run a controlled A/B benchmark comparing Redwood Inference against the hyperscaler endpoint you referenced (Hyperscaler X), using your sample corpus and the same model family you specified. We'll report p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and sustained throughput at different batch sizes.
- Data/constraints: please confirm that the sample corpus you shared is the final set (or tell us if you have an updated version). Also confirm whether we should run tests with KV cache enabled and whether you want quantized model variants included.
- Proposed timeline: we'll run an initial A/B test tomorrow (Tue) and share a preliminary summary + CSVs by EOD Wed. If you'd like, we can do an extended run (24h sustained traffic) the following week.

Next steps: Reply to confirm the corpus and the cache/quantization preferences. I'll loop in Rishi (infra/bench lead) on the results for any deeper technical Qs.

Subject: Fwd: Redwood — preliminary A/B benchmark results (Redwood vs Hyperscaler X)

Hi Sam — forwarding the preliminary A/B run results. Files attached: globex-redwood-vs-hyperscaler-20260609.csv, p95-p99-latency-plot.png, and a short notes PDF with test configs. Summary below (all tests used your corpus and identical model architecture where possible):

Summary (median across three runs, 95% CI):
- p95 latency: Redwood = 95 ms | Hyperscaler X = 150 ms
- p99 latency: Redwood = 220 ms | Hyperscaler X = 380 ms
- First-token (cold) median: Redwood = 120 ms | Hyperscaler X = 260 ms
- Tokens/sec (sustained, single-node baseline): Redwood = 4,200 t/s | Hyperscaler X = 3,100 t/s
- Sustained throughput at 2k concurrent simulated qps (clustered run): Redwood sustained 85% of target with autoscale to reserved nodes; Hyperscaler hit 62% before queueing/backpressure.
- Cost-per-1k-tokens (raw infra estimate, not including networking or enterprise discounts): Redwood = $0.012/1k | Hyperscaler X = $0.018/1k

Notes / caveats:
- We ran two variants: quantized int8 and fp16. The numbers above are the best-performing variant in each vendor's pipeline (int8 where supported). Hyperscaler X's quantized path added ~15% latency compared to their fp16 path; Redwood's runtime shows smaller overhead for int8.
- KV cache was enabled for the sustained throughput runs; cold-start numbers are from fresh containers without warmed cache.
- We included tokenization-induced variability in the csv; see the attached CSV and plot for latency distributions (p50/p75/p90/p95/p99).
- Attached notes include exact engine versions, batch sizes, and input sequence length distributions.

Proposed next tests:
1) 24h sustained run with autoscaling and synthetic flash bursts (2k -> 6k qps) to validate tail behavior.
2) Dedicated cluster run (reserved capacity) to validate predictable throughput and failover scenarios.
3) Blinded summary generation for procurement (we can redact vendor headers and provide a templated export).

Let me know which of these you want prioritized; happy to schedule the Thu deep-dive.
